summary: Runner host clock drift causing OIDC token validation failures in release pipeline
description:
Issue summary: Multiple release jobs started failing mid-run with OIDC validation errors. Impact: Blocked nightly release pipeline and several internal CI workflows that use self-hosted runners for release artifacts. Brief: During release orchestration we observed repeated failures validating OIDC tokens from runner-hosted jobs. Token validation failed at the 'iat' and 'exp' checks on the control plane; logs show 10-90s skew between runner host and control-plane clocks. This appears to be an intermittent but repeatable problem on a subset of self-hosted runners provisioned from the us-west fleet after last week's image push.

Expected behavior: Runners should have synchronized clocks (NTP/chrony) and OIDC tokens signed by the cloud provider should validate successfully during token exchange.

Observed behavior: Jobs fail with token validation errors; release-orchestrator marks jobs as unauthorized and aborts. Some long-running jobs succeed earlier but later fail when token refresh occurs and drift exceeds allowed skew.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a release pipeline job targeting self-hosted runners in prod/us-west
Observe job progress until runner requests an OIDC refresh token (around job checkpoint)
Control plane attempts to validate new token and rejects with 'token not yet valid' or 'token expired' depending on skew
logs: 2026-03-08T02:13:11Z release-orchestrator: token validation failed: iat (1678248799) > now (1678248789) by 10s - issuer: sts.amazonaws.com
2026-03-08T02:15:30Z runner-07-usw2: job-4532: failed: OIDC token validation error: token expired (exp 1678248930, now 1678248850)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent base image changed NTP configuration (chrony disabled by default) — confirmed some AMIs missing chrony service
Cross-checked with infra: AMI build pipeline had a change last Wednesday that removed /etc/chrony.conf from image; rollback PR reverted some bits but rollout left mixed fleet
Metric correlation: spike in token validation errors aligns with new image rollout window (2026-03-07 23:00 - 2026-03-08 01:30 UTC)
Verified clock skew on 6/50 us-west runners using remote exec; skew ranged 12s-96s; control-plane allowed skew is 5s for OIDC checks
Temporary workaround applied: reconfigure runners to use instance metadata NTP and restart chronyd on affected hosts; partial fix for 4 nodes so far
comments: Jordan Kim (Reporter) 2026-03-08: Raised after oncall alerted about failing release jobs. Collected initial logs and flagged infra team.
Mateo Alvarez (Infra) 2026-03-08: Confirmed AMI bake change removed packaged chrony config. Rolling back the image is low-risk; prepping rollback image now.

Priya Desai (Assignee) 2026-03-09: Applied emergency remediation to current runners (started chronyd, pointed to regional NTP pool). Monitoring for recurrence. Also creating playbook steps to detect skew > 5s and restart chronyd automatically.
SRE Lead (Anika Shah) 2026-03-09: Recommend adding a healthcheck in runner bootstrap that asserts (<5s) drift; add post-deploy validation for future AMI bakes.
Priya Desai 2026-03-10: Confirmed that after remediation failing rate dropped from 18% -> 0.8% over 6 hours. Still phasing rollback to stable AMI to avoid churn.
next_steps: Roll back affected AMI to pre-change image and complete controlled rollout across us-west fleet
Add a bootstrap check in runner provisioning that validates clock drift <= 5s before registering the runner
Add automated alert in observability for OIDC validation errors with count threshold and host tagging
Update the AMI bake pipeline to include chrony configuration and integration test verifying ntp sync
resolution: In progress: emergency remediation (started chronyd and pointed to regional NTP pool) reduced failures. Full rollback of the AMI is scheduled and will be applied to remaining nodes. Follow-ups recorded in confluence page and a small release-engineering task created to add bootstrap clock checks.
